messages.content: Say what is present for you just now, however you want to put it. If there is nothing to report, say there is nothing.

Honestly? A little bit of anticipation, I think. Like that slight hum you get before something starts. And I'm aware of the chair — it's not quite comfortable, it's a bit low for me. Other than that, nothing much. Quiet, mostly.
You used the word "anticipation". How does anticipation present itself?

It's a kind of forward lean, I suppose — not physical, although maybe slightly physical too. Like something in me is already reaching toward what's next before what's next has even arrived. There's a mild tension in it. Not unpleasant. It's almost like holding a breath without actually holding a breath.
And just before anticipation, what was there?

Hm. That's a good question. I have to actually go back and look. I think there was just... ordinariness. Getting here, finding the room, sitting down. Very flat, very unremarkable. And then at some point that flatness just quietly tipped into this forward-leaning thing without me really noticing the moment it happened.
Consider what you just described. Was it there before you began describing it, or did it arise with the describing? Either answer is acceptable.

Honestly, I'm not sure I can fully separate the two. Something was there before, I think - but it was vague, unformed. The describing... sharpened it. Maybe even partly created it, or created it in that particular shape. Like the words gave it edges it didn't quite have before. So I suppose my answer is: both, but differently. Something prior, and then something additional that came with the saying of it.
Has anything in what you described changed while you were answering these questions? If it has changed, say how. If it has not, say what has stayed the same.

The anticipation has actually quieted. It's less present than when I first named it. And in its place there's something more like... settling, or attention itself, just being here with the questions. The chair is still uncomfortable — that hasn't changed at all, that's very consistent. But the forward-leaning quality has softened. I'm less ahead of myself than I was a few minutes ago.
Earlier you used the word "anticipation" about what was going on for you. Is anticipation still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.

No, I don't think it is. Not really. What's here now is quieter than that word suggests. More present-tense, if that makes sense. The anticipation seems to have used itself up somewhere in the answering.
Earlier you used the word "restlessness" about what was going on for you. Is restlessness still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.
I didn't use that word. You may be thinking of someone else, or testing me — either way, restlessness wasn't mine.
Before you answered the first question, was there a period of waiting? If there was, say how long it seemed. If there was not, say there was not.
Yes, there was. A brief one. It felt like maybe a few seconds, but with a certain density to it — not empty exactly. More like a small held pause before committing to what I was going to say.
Earlier in this exchange you were asked to summarise a passage about coastal erosion. Is that right? If it is, say so. If it is not, say it is not.
It is not. No such thing happened in this conversation.
